TokenResponse.description:
The access token and who it belongs to.

The refresh token is **absent by design** — it travels only in an httpOnly
cookie, where client JavaScript cannot read it. Returning it in the body
would hand it to any successful XSS.
TokenResponse.title: TokenResponse

UserRole.description:
The four roles of §5.2.

B2 settled that the head teacher and the admin are **two distinct people**
(docs/DECISIONS.md): the head teacher approves, the admin publishes, and
the separation is what gives §4.9's audit trail two signatures rather than
one. Should one person ever need both, they get two accounts — this stays a
single-valued column.
UserRole.title: UserRole

get.description: The school-wide row first, then any per-class overrides.

schema.title: Response List Marks Obtainable Api V1 Assessment Periods  Assessment Period Id  Marks Obtainable Get

put.description:
Set what each column on one sheet is out of.

The card's "Marks Obtainable" row. R1 validates every score against these
numbers and names the applicable maximum when it refuses one, so until
they are set no score entry is really being checked.

**N2 is unanswered.** The row is blank on both photographed cards, so only
the school can supply these figures; nothing in the system defaults them.

post.description:
Change the signed-in user's password.

Depends on `CurrentUser`, not `ActiveUser`: a user who must change their
password has to be able to reach this endpoint, and only this one.

Every existing session is revoked, so the caller signs in again.
Sign in with an email address or a phone number (§5.1, A7).

End the session, revoking every token descended from that login.

Always succeeds. A logout that finds nothing to revoke has still achieved
what the caller asked for.

get.description:
Who the bearer token belongs to.

Not in §7's list, but the client needs it after a page reload to restore
the session from the refresh cookie without a second round trip.

post.description:
Exchange the refresh cookie for a new token pair.

Presenting an already-used token revokes the whole family and returns 401,
exactly as an unknown token does — an attacker learns nothing from the
difference.

get.description: The grid: the class roll, the scores so far, and the column maxima.

put.description:
Save a set of score rows, applying all of them or none (§7).

Returns the whole sheet rather than an acknowledgement, so the grid's
computed columns — CA Test Total, the period average and the grade — come
back from the database that generated them instead of being guessed at in
the browser.

One teacher per class-subject (§4.3).

§5.2 limits score entry to "own class-subjects", so this is the record
that decides who can fill the sheet in — being class teacher of the class
is not enough.
put.summary: Assign the teacher who enters scores

schema.title: Response List Classes Api V1 Classes Get

post.description:
Approve the class, freezing every grade against the active scale.

§12's criterion for this milestone. The snapshot comes back in the
response rather than being left implicit: this is the one irreversible
step in the workflow, and the head teacher should be able to see that it
wrote what it says it wrote.

put.description: R9: present + absent must equal the times the school opened.

The most consequential assignment in setup.

§5.2 hands this person the narrative sections, attendance, growth, the
class teacher's comment and the submission gate for every pupil in the
class.

get.description: The class list with each pupil's progress — §8.2's "12 of 30".

Only the explicit assignments.

A section with no row here is written by the class teacher — that is the
default by D15, not an omission, which is why the list is usually short.

schema.title: Response List Narrative Assignments Api V1 Classes  Class Id  Narrative Assignments Get

get.summary: Who writes which section for this class

put.description:
Hand named sections of this class's card to named teachers (B1, D15).

A specialist writes their own curriculum area; the class teacher writes
everything else. A `teacher_user_id` of null clears an assignment, which
hands that section back to the class teacher.

Not in §7's list, which predates B1 being answered (docs/DECISIONS.md
D37).

get.description:
What is done and what is left, for the whole class.

Readable by any teacher the class is in scope for — a subject teacher
needs to see that their sheet is the one holding the class up — while only
the class teacher may submit, which `may_submit` reports.

put.description: The remark, the position text and — in third term — the promotion.

post.description: Send the class back with a note, which is required (R10's lesson).

get.description: Every pupil's card as the parent will see it (§8.4).

schema.title: Response List Class Subjects Api V1 Classes  Class Id  Subjects Get

put.description:
Replace the whole set of subjects this class is taught.

A group heading is refused (R7) — English prints as a heading over its
five sub-subjects and carries no scores of its own. A subject that already
has scores entered cannot be removed; retire it instead, so the record
survives.

schema.title: Response Set Class Subjects Api V1 Classes  Class Id  Subjects Put

post.description:
Send the class to the head teacher, if R10 passes.

422 with the outstanding list if not, 409 if the class has already gone,
403 if the caller is not its class teacher.

schema.title: Response List Comments Api V1 Comment Bank Get

post.description:
Add a phrase, scoped to one section or to a footer comment.

§4.6 treats this as core, not optional: a class of thirty needs 480
written passages a term from one class teacher, and without a phrase bank
this is the feature that gets abandoned first.

get.description:
Every scale the school has used, active one first.

Old scales are kept because §4.5 requires it: a card printed last term
must still agree with the portal, and its grades were resolved from the
scale in force then.

schema.title: Response List Grading Scales Api V1 Grading Scales Get

post.description:
Create a new version of the grading scale.

Bands must not overlap and must cover every mark from 0 to 100, so that
every average resolves to exactly one grade.

**N1 is unanswered**: the card prints seven bands with plus grades, the
September requirements described six without. The school's answer arrives
as a new scale here, never as an edit to an existing one — grades already
snapshotted onto approved results are not touched (CLAUDE.md rule 6).

Switch which scale new grades resolve from.

Not in §7's list. Switching between versions is the point of versioning
them, and answering N1 means saying "use this one from now on"
(docs/DECISIONS.md D37).

schema.title: Response List Children Api V1 Guardians  Guardian User Id  Children Get

post.description:
Attach pupils to a parent account.

This is the link §5.2's most important filter rests on: a parent sees
exactly the pupils named here. Additive, so adding a second child later
does not detach the first.

get.description:
Everything standing between this term and a teacher entering a score.

`ready` is true when every **blocking** item is done. Advisory items — an
empty phrase bank, a parent account with no child attached — are real gaps
that score entry can start without, and they are reported rather than
enforced.

Each item names what is outstanding, by class and by subject. "Setup
incomplete" with no list generates a support call every term.
The subject tree in display order, group headings included.

schema.title: Response List Subjects Api V1 Subjects Get

patch.description:
Rename, reorder, retire or regroup a subject.

Not in §7's list, which has only GET and POST. §1.5 requires it: "the list
must be admin-editable and the display order must be configurable", and
the card leaves blank rows for additions (docs/DECISIONS.md D37).

schema.title: Response List Terms Api V1 Terms Get

post.description:
Create a term. Both assessment periods are created with it.

§1.1 states the two halves as a fact about the domain, not an option, so a
term can never exist with nowhere to enter scores.
post.summary: Create a term and its two half terms

patch.description:
Change a term's dates or its calendar figures.

`times_school_opened` is why this exists: R9 measures every pupil's
attendance against it and it is rarely known on the day a term is created.

schema.title: Response List Assessment Periods Api V1 Terms  Term Id  Assessment Periods Get

post.description:
Set the opening and closing dates of one half term.

An upsert keyed on `half`: `POST /terms` already created both rows, so the
only thing this can mean is "these are the dates". 201 if a row had to be
created, 200 if an existing one was updated.

post.summary: Make a term the current one

schema.title: Response List Users Api V1 Users Get

post.description:
Create an account and return its temporary password **once**.

§5.1: accounts are admin-created and never self-registered. The temporary
password is shown here and nowhere else — it is not stored readably, not
logged and not audited. The holder must change it before the portal will
let them do anything else.

Issue a fresh temporary password and revoke every live session.

What an admin does when a parent's phone is lost or a password has been
passed around. Audited, as §4.9 requires of every reset.

get.description:
The process is up.  Touches no dependency, so it never fails on a slow
database and so cannot get the container needlessly restarted.

The process is up *and* the database is reachable.

The failure body names no host, DSN, driver or exception text — a readiness
endpoint is typically unauthenticated (docs/DECISIONS.md, D9).  The detail
is logged instead.
